stem: Transaminase acts on which substrate?
rationale: Transamination, catalyzed by a transaminase, is the first catabolic reaction of most protein amino acids.

stem: Which substrate does glutaminase act on in the reaction that forms glutamate and ammonium?
rationale: Glutaminase (EC 3.5.1.2) catalyzes the reaction of glutamine and water to form glutamate and ammonium.
citation: chapter_29_catabolism_of_the_carbon_skeletons_of_amino_acids — Catabolism of the Carbon Skeletons of Amino Acids > TRANSAMINATION TYPICALLY INITIATES AMINO ACID CATABOLISM > Glutamine & Glutamate Form α-Ketoglutarate

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of metabolic block?
rationale: The metabolic block in type I hyperprolinemia is at proline dehydrogenase. There is no associated impairment of hydroxyproline catabolism in type I hyperprolinemia.
citation: chapter_29_catabolism_of_the_carbon_skeletons_of_amino_acids — Catabolism of the Carbon Skeletons of Amino Acids > TRANSAMINATION TYPICALLY INITIATES AMINO ACID CATABOLISM > Proline

stem: Formimino is converted into which substance?
rationale: The formimino group is transferred to tetrahydrofolate, forming glutamate.
citation: chapter_29_catabolism_of_the_carbon_skeletons_of_amino_acids — Catabolism of the Carbon Skeletons of Amino Acids > TRANSAMINATION TYPICALLY INITIATES AMINO ACID CATABOLISM > Histidine

stem: Urolithiasis can develop as a complication of which condition related to glyoxylate metabolism?
rationale: The oxidation of glyoxylate to oxalate leads to urolithiasis, nephrocalcinosis, and early mortality from renal failure or hypertension in primary hyperoxaluria.

citation: chapter_29_catabolism_of_the_carbon_skeletons_of_amino_acids — Catabolism of the Carbon Skeletons of Amino Acids > TRANSAMINATION TYPICALLY INITIATES AMINO ACID CATABOLISM > Histidine

stem: Renal failure can develop as a complication of which condition related to glyoxylate metabolism?
rationale: The oxidation of glyoxylate to oxalate leads to urolithiasis, nephrocalcinosis, and early mortality from renal failure or hypertension in primary hyperoxaluria.
citation: chapter_29_catabolism_of_the_carbon_skeletons_of_amino_acids — Catabolism of the Carbon Skeletons of Amino Acids > TRANSAMINATION TYPICALLY INITIATES AMINO ACID CATABOLISM > Histidine

stem: Hypertension can develop as a complication of which condition related to glyoxylate metabolism?
rationale: The oxidation of glyoxylate to oxalate leads to urolithiasis, nephrocalcinosis, and early mortality from renal failure or hypertension in primary hyperoxaluria.
citation: chapter_29_catabolism_of_the_carbon_skeletons_of_amino_acids — Catabolism of the Carbon Skeletons of Amino Acids > TRANSAMINATION TYPICALLY INITIATES AMINO ACID CATABOLISM > Histidine

stem: Ammonia-forming aminomethyltransferase acts on which substrate?
rationale: The three enzymes in the glycine cleavage complex are glycine dehydrogenase (decarboxylating), an ammonia-forming aminomethyltransferase, and dihydrolipoamide dehydrogenase.
citation: chapter_29_catabolism_of_the_carbon_skeletons_of_amino_acids — Catabolism of the Carbon Skeletons of Amino Acids > TRANSAMINATION TYPICALLY INITIATES AMINO ACID CATABOLISM > Histidine

stem: Dihydrolipoamide dehydrogenase acts on which substrate?
rationale: The three enzymes in the glycine cleavage complex are glycine dehydrogenase (decarboxylating), an ammonia-forming aminomethyltransferase, and dihydrolipoamide dehydrogenase.
citation: chapter_29_catabolism_of_the_carbon_skeletons_of_amino_acids — Catabolism of the Carbon Skeletons of Amino Acids > TRANSAMINATION TYPICALLY INITIATES AMINO ACID CATABOLISM > Histidine

stem: Serine is converted into which substance?
rationale: Serine catabolism merges with that of glycine after serine is converted to glycine.
citation: chapter_29_catabolism_of_the_carbon_skeletons_of_amino_acids — Catabolism of the Carbon Skeletons of Amino Acids > TRANSAMINATION TYPICALLY INITIATES AMINO ACID CATABOLISM > Serine

stem: Tetrahydrofolate requires which substance?
rationale: Tetrahydrofolate acts as a cofactor in the interconversion of serine and glycine (Figure 29--6).
citation: chapter_29_catabolism_of_the_carbon_skeletons_of_amino_acids — Catabolism of the Carbon Skeletons of Amino Acids > TRANSAMINATION TYPICALLY INITIATES AMINO ACID CATABOLISM > Serine

stem: Cysteine is converted into which substance?
rationale: Two pathways convert cysteine to pyruvate (Figure 29-8).
citation: chapter_29_catabolism_of_the_carbon_skeletons_of_amino_acids — Catabolism of the Carbon Skeletons of Amino Acids > TRANSAMINATION TYPICALLY INITIATES AMINO ACID CATABOLISM > Cystine & Cysteine

stem: Acute renal failure can develop as a complication of which condition?
rationale: Early mortality from acute renal failure is associated with cystinosis.
citation: chapter_29_catabolism_of_the_carbon_skeletons_of_amino_acids — Catabolism of the Carbon Skeletons of Amino Acids > TRANSAMINATION TYPICALLY INITIATES AMINO ACID CATABOLISM > (Cysteine) (Homocysteine)

stem: Tyrosine is converted into which substance?
rationale: Tyrosine is transaminated to p-hydroxyphenylpyruvate. P-hydroxyphenylpyruvate is converted to homogentisate.
citation: chapter_29_catabolism_of_the_carbon_skeletons_of_amino_acids — Catabolism of the Carbon Skeletons of Amino Acids > TRANSAMINATION TYPICALLY INITIATES AMINO ACID CATABOLISM > Tyrosine

stem: P-hydroxyphenylpyruvate is converted into which substance?
rationale: P-hydroxyphenylpyruvate is converted to homogentisate. Homogentisate is transformed into maleylacetoacetate.
citation: chapter_29_catabolism_of_the_carbon_skeletons_of_amino_acids — Catabolism of the Carbon Skeletons of Amino Acids > TRANSAMINATION TYPICALLY INITIATES AMINO ACID CATABOLISM > Tyrosine

stem: Fumarylacetoacetate is converted into which substance?
rationale: Fumarylacetoacetate is broken down into fumarate and acetoacetate. Fumarate and acetoacetate are ultimately converted into acetyl-CoA and acetate.
citation: chapter_29_catabolism_of_the_carbon_skeletons_of_amino_acids — Catabolism of the Carbon Skeletons of Amino Acids > TRANSAMINATION TYPICALLY INITIATES AMINO ACID CATABOLISM > Tyrosine

stem: Fumarate is converted into which substance?
rationale: Fumarate and acetoacetate are ultimately converted into acetyl-CoA and acetate.
citation: chapter_29_catabolism_of_the_carbon_skeletons_of_amino_acids — Catabolism of the Carbon Skeletons of Amino Acids > TRANSAMINATION TYPICALLY INITIATES AMINO ACID CATABOLISM > Tyrosine

stem: Acetoacetate is converted into which substance?
rationale: Fumarate and acetoacetate are ultimately converted into acetyl-CoA and acetate.
citation: chapter_29_catabolism_of_the_carbon_skeletons_of_amino_acids — Catabolism of the Carbon Skeletons of Amino Acids > TRANSAMINATION TYPICALLY INITIATES AMINO ACID CATABOLISM > Tyrosine

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of tyrosinosis?
rationale: Type I tyrosinemia, also known as tyrosinosis, is caused by a defect in fumarylacetoacetate hydrolase. Therapy for type I tyrosinemia involves a diet low in tyrosine and phenylalanine.
citation: chapter_29_catabolism_of_the_carbon_skeletons_of_amino_acids — Catabolism of the Carbon Skeletons of Amino Acids > TRANSAMINATION TYPICALLY INITIATES AMINO ACID CATABOLISM > Tyrosine

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of type II tyrosinemia?
rationale: Type II tyrosinemia, or Richner-Hanhart syndrome, results from a defect in tyrosine aminotransferase. Neonatal tyrosinemia is due to lowered activity of p-hydroxyphenylpyruvate hydroxylase.
citation: chapter_29_catabolism_of_the_carbon_skeletons_of_amino_acids — Catabolism of the Carbon Skeletons of Amino Acids > TRANSAMINATION TYPICALLY INITIATES AMINO ACID CATABOLISM > Tyrosine

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of death in untreated type I tyrosinemia?
rationale: Untreated type I tyrosinemia can lead to death from liver failure. Type II tyrosinemia, or Richner-Hanhart syndrome, results from a defect in tyrosine aminotransferase.
citation: chapter_29_catabolism_of_the_carbon_skeletons_of_amino_acids — Catabolism of the Carbon Skeletons of Amino Acids > TRANSAMINATION TYPICALLY INITIATES AMINO ACID CATABOLISM > Tyrosine

stem: Which agent is used in the management of type II tyrosinemia?
rationale: Therapy for type II tyrosinemia and neonatal tyrosinemia involves a diet low in protein.
citation: chapter_29_catabolism_of_the_carbon_skeletons_of_amino_acids — Catabolism of the Carbon Skeletons of Amino Acids > TRANSAMINATION TYPICALLY INITIATES AMINO ACID CATABOLISM > Tyrosine

stem: Which agent is used in the management of tyrosinemia?
rationale: Therapy for type II tyrosinemia and neonatal tyrosinemia involves a diet low in protein.
citation: chapter_29_catabolism_of_the_carbon_skeletons_of_amino_acids — Catabolism of the Carbon Skeletons of Amino Acids > TRANSAMINATION TYPICALLY INITIATES AMINO ACID CATABOLISM > Tyrosine

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of ochronosis?
rationale: Ochronosis results from the oxidation of homogentisate to benzoquinone acetate, which polymerizes and binds to connective tissue.
citation: chapter_29_catabolism_of_the_carbon_skeletons_of_amino_acids — Catabolism of the Carbon Skeletons of Amino Acids > TRANSAMINATION TYPICALLY INITIATES AMINO ACID CATABOLISM > Tyrosine

stem: Phenylalanine is converted into which substance?
rationale: Phenylalanine is first converted to tyrosine (see Figure 27--11).
citation: chapter_29_catabolism_of_the_carbon_skeletons_of_amino_acids — Catabolism of the Carbon Skeletons of Amino Acids > TRANSAMINATION TYPICALLY INITIATES AMINO ACID CATABOLISM > Phenylalanine

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of hyperphenylalaninemias?
rationale: Hyperphenylalaninemias arise from defects in dihydrobiopterin biosynthesis.
citation: chapter_29_catabolism_of_the_carbon_skeletons_of_amino_acids — Catabolism of the Carbon Skeletons of Amino Acids > TRANSAMINATION TYPICALLY INITIATES AMINO ACID CATABOLISM > Phenylalanine

stem: Glutaryl-CoA is converted into which substance?
rationale: Decarboxylation of glutaryl-CoA to crotonyl-CoA is reaction 6. Defects involving the second activity are accompanied by elevated levels of blood saccharopine.
citation: chapter_29_catabolism_of_the_carbon_skeletons_of_amino_acids — Catabolism of the Carbon Skeletons of Amino Acids > TRANSAMINATION TYPICALLY INITIATES AMINO ACID CATABOLISM > Lysine

stem: Tryptophan is converted into which substance?
rationale: Tryptophan is degraded to amphibolic intermediates via the kynurenine-anthranilate pathway (Figure 29--15).
citation: chapter_29_catabolism_of_the_carbon_skeletons_of_amino_acids — Catabolism of the Carbon Skeletons of Amino Acids > TRANSAMINATION TYPICALLY INITIATES AMINO ACID CATABOLISM > Tryptophan

stem: EC 1.13.11.11 acts on which substrate?
rationale: Tryptophan 2,3-dioxygenase, EC 1.13.11.11 (tryptophan pyrrolase) opens the indole ring, incorporates molecular oxygen, and forms N-formylkynurenine.
citation: chapter_29_catabolism_of_the_carbon_skeletons_of_amino_acids — Catabolism of the Carbon Skeletons of Amino Acids > TRANSAMINATION TYPICALLY INITIATES AMINO ACID CATABOLISM > Tryptophan

stem: Which substrate does kynurenine formylase act on?
rationale: Hydrolytic removal of the formyl group of N-formylkynurenine, catalyzed by kynurenine formylase (EC 3.5.1.9), produces kynurenine.
citation: chapter_29_catabolism_of_the_carbon_skeletons_of_amino_acids — Catabolism of the Carbon Skeletons of Amino Acids > TRANSAMINATION TYPICALLY INITIATES AMINO ACID CATABOLISM > Tryptophan

stem: What substance is required by EC 3.7.1.3?
rationale: Kynureninase (EC 3.7.1.3) requires pyridoxal phosphate.
citation: chapter_29_catabolism_of_the_carbon_skeletons_of_amino_acids — Catabolism of the Carbon Skeletons of Amino Acids > TRANSAMINATION TYPICALLY INITIATES AMINO ACID CATABOLISM > Tryptophan

stem: What is a recognized cause of Hartnup disease?
rationale: Hartnup disease reflects impaired intestinal and renal transport of tryptophan and other neutral amino acids.
citation: chapter_29_catabolism_of_the_carbon_skeletons_of_amino_acids — Catabolism of the Carbon Skeletons of Amino Acids > TRANSAMINATION TYPICALLY INITIATES AMINO ACID CATABOLISM > Tryptophan

stem: Indole is converted into which substance?
rationale: Indole derivatives of unabsorbed tryptophan formed by intestinal bacteria are excreted.
citation: chapter_29_catabolism_of_the_carbon_skeletons_of_amino_acids — Catabolism of the Carbon Skeletons of Amino Acids > TRANSAMINATION TYPICALLY INITIATES AMINO ACID CATABOLISM > Tryptophan

stem: Propionyl-CoA is converted into which substance?
rationale: Propionyl-CoA is converted to succinyl-CoA through reactions 2, 3, and 4 (Figure 19-2).
citation: chapter_29_catabolism_of_the_carbon_skeletons_of_amino_acids — Catabolism of the Carbon Skeletons of Amino Acids > TRANSAMINATION TYPICALLY INITIATES AMINO ACID CATABOLISM > Methionine

stem: What is a recognized cause of histidinemia?
rationale: Histidine ammonia lyase (histidase) deficiency leads to histidinemia and urocanic acidemia.
citation: chapter_29_catabolism_of_the_carbon_skeletons_of_amino_acids — Catabolism of the Carbon Skeletons of Amino Acids > METABOLIC DISORDERS OF BRANCHED-CHAIN AMINO ACID CATABOLISM

stem: What is a recognized cause of phenylketonuria?
rationale: Metabolic disorders of phenylalanine catabolism include PKU and several hyperphenylalaninemias.
citation: chapter_29_catabolism_of_the_carbon_skeletons_of_amino_acids — Catabolism of the Carbon Skeletons of Amino Acids

stem: What is a recognized cause of hyperlysinemia-ammonemia?
rationale: Metabolic diseases of lysine catabolism include periodic and persistent forms of hyperlysinemia-ammonemia.
citation: chapter_29_catabolism_of_the_carbon_skeletons_of_amino_acids — Catabolism of the Carbon Skeletons of Amino Acids

stem: What is a recognized cause of hypervalinemia?
rationale: Metabolic disorders of branched-chain amino acid catabolism include hypervalinemia, maple syrup urine disease, intermittent branched-chain ketonuria, isovaleric acidemia, and methylmalonic aciduria.
citation: chapter_29_catabolism_of_the_carbon_skeletons_of_amino_acids — Catabolism of the Carbon Skeletons of Amino Acids
